title: Glutamine binding and sodium coordination reveal the transport mechanism of y⁺LAT1/CD98hc
task: Determine transport mechanism of y⁺LAT1/CD98hc amino acid transporter
key_results: Cryo-EM structure at 3.4 Å reveals non-canonical glutamine binding via Cys320; identified Na⁺-binding tetrad (Asn49–Ser131–Gly323–Ser327) enabling Na⁺-dependent neutral amino acid transport; cationic substrates bypass Na⁺ requirement
comments: The structural insight into dual transport mechanisms (Na⁺-dependent for neutral, Na⁺-independent for cationic substrates) elegantly explains LPI etiology and substrate selectivity.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Na⁺ forms a tetrad binding site that enables neutral amino acid transport
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; Na⁺-binding tetrad identified and validated by mutagenesis and kinetics

hypotheses.hypothesis: Cationic substrates replace Na⁺ role through electrostatic interactions
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; L-arginine occupies same locus with charged side chain enabling Na⁺-independent exchange

hypotheses.hypothesis: Glu128 is critical for inward-facing conformational transitions
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; mutagenesis revealed key role in transport cycle

title: PDGF-BB and bFGF repress Kai1 in pericytes through Src–DNMT-associated promoter methylation and lysosomal trafficking
task: Elucidate how PDGF-BB and bFGF suppress pericyte Kai1 via Src–DNMT-mediated promoter methylation and lysosomal trafficking

comments: The dual-layer regulation (transcriptional + post-translational) explains Kai1's selective loss in angiogenic microenvironments; this VEGF-independent mechanism may explain therapeutic escape from anti-VEGF strategies.
